narrative.summary: The deployer identity resolves to a single EOA and is shared with the dormant dex km, so a compromise is not a small-dex problem. The same address also runs Kinetiq's kmHYPE staking contract; no dex-admin path was found in it.
narrative.detail: About $6.4M to $6.7M open interest and 24 listed assets at promotion on 2026-09-17; km showed zero. The deployer address carries a proxy to Kinetiq's HIP3StakingManager. A first read suggested a second root-control path, but the verified source shows every CoreWriter call is a staking or trading helper, so nothing was folded into the score; the earlier finding notes a raw-action passthrough was not fully ruled out, though the ABI suggests none. The API wallet can only be set through EXManager, which needs a signature from exWalletAdmin, a plain EOA. The haltTrading and setOracle sub-deployers are plain keys. Stored under a derived key.

reproduce.note: this RPC cannot replay the block of the build (it ignores the block tag, or no longer serves old state): the call reproduces the current value, not the one of the build; compare the composite and lastUpdated with this page

cheapest_fix.what: a stronger admin setup (admin power spread beyond one key, or checked by others)

main_gap.requirement: Admin power is not a bare key
main_gap.reason: One key, or a tiny group, can change it

independent_read.why: no code at this address on the chain's mainnet: a derived identifier for a native (non-EVM) entity such as HyperCore, or a contract that lives on another chain (a rollup's own L1 contracts); nothing for this reader to compare here
